newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Toan Chay, moderate who may become new Cambodia PM.
newsitem.headline: Toan Chay, moderate who may become new Cambodia PM.

text.p: Toan Chay, a top candidate to replace Cambodia's ousted first prime minister, has stood out as a sophisticated military man and straight-talking moderate in the country's turbulent political scene.

By turns a dentistry student, military pilot and provincial governor, the 55-year-old Toan Chay has consistently supported King Norodom Sihanouk but is known to dislike the monarch's son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, analysts said on Tuesday.
For disgruntled royalists tired of Ranariddh's sagging leadership, the popular Toan Chay, who broke with the prince in April, was once viewed as a beacon of hope for the royalist FUNCINPEC party.

But with the ouster of Ranariddh by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on July 7, the party has been gutted and Toan Chay, a member of FUNCINPEC since its inception, will likely prove to be little more than a stand-in for the ousted first prime minister, analysts said.
"To survive, he will have to be very flexible to Hun Sen's desires," said one foreign analyst. "He will be there to maintain the alliance, but to do what?"
In the interview published on Tuesday in the Japanese newspaper Yomiuri Shimbun, Toan Chay sharply criticised Ranariddh.
"The prince is fond of living abroad. I do not think he is capable of leading efforts to rebuild the nation," Toan Chay said.
Toan Chay said all members of the FUNCINPEC party were now willing to cooperate with Hun Sen and the return of royalist Foreign Minister Ung Huot would add to Hun Sen's efforts to unite the country.

"(Foreign Minister) Ung Huot is a remarkable person and an old friend of mine. I am delighted he is back. The only person within the FUNCINPEC party rejecting cooperation with Hun Sen is Ranariddh himself," he said.

Toan Chay, an army general and governor of the northern province of Siem Reap, stepped into the limelight in April, when he broke with Ranariddh over fears that the prince, bogged down in a worsening political battle with Hun Sen, would not be able to lead the party effectively in general elections next year.
Toan Chay called for the removal of Ranariddh as party president, prompting FUNCINPEC to expel him and other dissidents from the party later that month.
In June Toan Chay convened a congress of a splinter group of royalists, who elected him president of their FUNCINPEC faction. Ranariddh at the time dismissed the rebels' move as meaningless.
It was not the first time that Toan Chay apparently stood on principle.

He was one of the first figures to organise resistance to the Khmer Rouge, architects of the 1975-79 "killing fields" regime, choosing as his mascot the Kleang Moeung, a mythical creature that sacrifices itself to give strength to others.

After the Vietnamese invaded and overthrew the Khmer Rouge in 1979, Toan Chay, who had trained as a pilot in the United States, was a fiercely pro-Sihanouk chief of staff in FUNCINPEC's anti-Vietnamese guerrilla army.
After U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, he briefly served as vice minister of interior before taking the post of governor in his birthplace of Siem Reap.
But he was never a member of parliament -- and that may prove his biggest obstacle in the coming weeks.
Toan Chay has expressed willingness to take the job of first prime minister, but the constitution says a prime minister must be a member of the National Assembly.

Toan Chay told the Yomiuri Shimbun that the party must first hold a convention to choose him as a candidate to succeed Ranariddh as party leader. After that, parliament must formally approve him, a process which could take about a month, he said.

Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed a coalition government after a U.N.-run election in May 1993. Hun Sen has said he does not want the job of first prime minister and called on FUNCINPEC members to choose a new person for the post.
